key_insight: JECT addresses the “context shortcut” in chest CT learning by making the encoder predict report content, encouraging it to represent findings that surrounding anatomy cannot predict.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support chest CT classification, finding localization, and risk prediction, but the abstract does not establish clinical readiness.
method: Condition masked-region feature prediction on the radiology report.
Train the encoder to predict anatomical report sections from the unmasked scan.
Apply prediction objectives at every stage of a hierarchical 3D encoder.
evidence_signal: Trained from scratch on 173k CT volumes, JECT reportedly matched current CT foundation models across classification, retrieval, and nodule malignancy tasks, and task-specific lung-cancer risk models after fine-tuning.
watch_item: Report conditioning alone added little encoder benefit in this setup; implementation should preserve the text-target objective rather than assume report access is sufficient.
paper_title: JECT: Addressing the Context Shortcut in Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for Chest CT
